This is the primary condition for this resource.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "Accepted"

Possible reasons for this condition to be Unknown are:

* "Pending"

operator_config.name: RewriteReasonAccepted
operator_config.doc:
RewriteReasonAccepted indicates the rewrite is valid, non-conflicting,
and has been successfully applied to the inference pool.

operator_config.name: RewriteReasonPending

RewriteReasonPending is the initial state, and indicates that the
controller has not yet reconciled the InferenceModelRewrite.

operator_config.name: ObjectiveConditionAccepted

ObjectiveConditionAccepted indicates if the objective config is accepted, and if not, why.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "Accepted"

Possible reasons for this condition to be Unknown are:

* "Pending"

operator_config.name: AddToScheme
operator_config.doc:
AddToScheme adds all types of this clientset into the given scheme. This allows composition
of clientsets, like in:

	import (
	  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
	  clientsetscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	  aggregatorclientsetscheme "k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/client/clientset_generated/clientset/scheme"
	)

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

operator_config.name: metricsShutdownTimeout
operator_config.doc:
metricsShutdownTimeout bounds the Prometheus /metrics server's shutdown.
Scrapes are short; a small budget is enough and keeps process exit prompt.

operator_config.name: evictionEngineReclaimBudget
operator_config.doc:
evictionEngineReclaimBudget covers the engine-side abort and KV garbage-collection time
between a revoked request's stream termination and the freed capacity appearing in scraped
metrics.

operator_config.name: evictionLeadingSensorGrace
operator_config.doc:
evictionLeadingSensorGrace covers scheduling jitter for sensors whose gauge updates in the
same event chain as the confirmation (a few dispatch ticks).

operator_config.name: metricsShutdownTimeout
operator_config.doc:
metricsShutdownTimeout bounds graceful shutdown of the metrics server so a
scraper holding a connection at process exit cannot block termination.

operator_config.name: debounceDelay
operator_config.doc: debounceDelay wait for events to settle before reloading

operator_config.name: BodyByteLimit
operator_config.doc:
BodyByteLimit is the max limit of 62Kb per streamed chunk.
Certain envoy implementations set a max limit of 64Kb per streamed chunk, intentionally setting this lower for a safe margin.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonEvicted
operator_config.doc:
Evicted — request was dispatched to an inference server and then killed.
The generic "evicted" reason is the current default used by ImmediateResponseEvictor.Evict().
The specific sub-reasons are forward-looking for when EvictN() callers specify why they're evicting.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
RequestDroppedReasonHeaderKey is the HTTP response header that communicates the specific
reason the EPP dropped a request.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonSaturated
operator_config.doc: Rejected — request never reached an inference server.

operator_config.name: atomicLevel
operator_config.doc:
atomicLevel is shared between InitSetupLogging and InitLogging so the log
level can be adjusted after the controller-runtime delegation is fulfilled.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessIDLabelLimit
operator_config.doc:
Fairness IDs are populated from a client request header (or an agent-identity
attribute), so their cardinality is not operator-bounded. They label
per-request, flow-control, and plugin metrics; without a cap, every distinct
fairness ID ever observed permanently grows the time series set. The cap
defaults to DefaultFairnessIDLabelLimit and collapses excess values to
OverflowValue. A cap of 0 folds every ID onto the single overflow series.

operator_config.name: OverflowValue
operator_config.doc:
OverflowValue is the label value emitted by BoundedLabel.Bound once the cap
fills. Callers that need to distinguish an "unknown" (empty) request-derived
label value from the cap-overflow value should keep their own sentinel and
gate empty inputs at the wrapper layer.

operator_config.name: GeneralLatencyBuckets
operator_config.doc:
GeneralLatencyBuckets is a request-duration histogram ladder from 5ms to
1 hour. Every llm-d component that emits a request-duration histogram
reuses it so PromQL translates cleanly across components.

operator_config.name: LLMDRouterEndpointPickerSubsystem
operator_config.doc: LLMDRouterEndpointPickerSubsystem is the subsystem for llm-d router endpoint picker metrics.

operator_config.name: TokenCountBuckets
operator_config.doc:
TokenCountBuckets is a token-count histogram ladder from 1 to ~1M in
powers of two (with 1 as the low end and 8 as the second entry). Input
and cached-prompt token histograms across llm-d components share this
shape.

operator_config.name: GenAIRequestIDKey

operator_config.name: GenAIRequestModelKey

operator_config.name: LLMDEPPPDDisaggregationUsedKey

operator_config.name: LLMDEPPPDPrefillPodAddressKey

operator_config.name: LLMDEPPProfileHandlerTotalProfilesKey

operator_config.name: LLMDEPPScorerEndpointsScoredKey

operator_config.doc: LogKeySpanID is the structured-log field carrying the active span ID.

operator_config.name: LogKeyTraceID
operator_config.doc:
LogKeyTraceID is the structured-log field carrying the active trace ID.
It matches the W3C trace-context identifier used across the llm-d stack
so logs from every component can be queried uniformly by trace.

operator_config.name: otlpProtocolEnv
operator_config.doc: otlpProtocolEnv are the variables that select the OTLP transport, per-signal first.

operator_config.name: DataParallelEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: DataParallelEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port> for Data Parallel

operator_config.name: EncoderEndpointsHeader
operator_config.doc: EncoderEndpointsHeader is the header name used to indicate Encoder workers <ip:port> list

operator_config.name: InferencePoolAPIGroup
operator_config.doc: InferencePoolAPIGroup is the default InferencePool API group

operator_config.name: KVCacheSourceHeader
operator_config.doc:
KVCacheSourceHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port> holding
the most cached prefix KV blocks for the request, to pull from over the P2P connector
instead of recomputing them

operator_config.name: PreferHeader
operator_config.doc:
PreferHeader is the standard HTTP "Prefer" header (RFC 7240). EPP
receives header keys lowercased.

operator_config.name: PreferIfAvailable
operator_config.doc:
PreferIfAvailable is the preference token the coordinator sets to mark a
request as a speculative early-decode attempt: route to a decode worker
only if its KV cache already covers the prompt (at least partially); otherwise EPP surfaces
412 Precondition Failed so the coordinator restarts the pipeline.

operator_config.name: PrefillEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: PrefillEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate Prefill worker <ip:port>

operator_config.name: maxValueLen
operator_config.doc:
maxValueLen caps a logged header value. Longer values are truncated so a
verbose metadata header does not dominate the log line.

operator_config.name: BytesPerMB
operator_config.doc: BytesPerMB is the number of bytes in one megabyte.

operator_config.name: DefaultMaxRequestBodySize
operator_config.doc:
DefaultMaxRequestBodySize is the default cap for server.max_request_body_size,
in megabytes. It is generous enough to accommodate multimodal requests that
inline images as data: URIs; text-only deployments can lower it.

operator_config.name: DefaultECConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultECConnectorName is the EC connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to ec-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: DefaultKVConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultKVConnectorName is the KV connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to kv-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: maxRedactDepth
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactDepth caps redactStrings recursion so a deeply nested adversarial
body cannot drive it toward the 500-level encoding/json limit on a trace log.

operator_config.name: maxRedactElems
operator_config.doc: maxRedactElems caps how many array elements are kept before a count marker.

operator_config.name: maxRedactRawBodyLen
operator_config.doc: maxRedactRawBodyLen bounds a non-JSON body logged verbatim.

operator_config.name: maxRedactStringLen
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactStringLen is the longest JSON string value kept verbatim; longer
values are replaced with a marker so tensor blobs, base64, and URLs do not
drown out the structural fields.

operator_config.name: maxModelLabelValues
operator_config.doc:
The model_name label is populated from the request body, which no
coordinator config validates against a closed set. Prometheus *Vec types
never evict label combinations, so an unbounded number of distinct model
names would grow the time series set without limit and exhaust memory. The
cap matches EPP's cap for the same reason and for consistency between the
two components.

operator_config.name: LLMDRouterCoordinatorSubsystem
operator_config.doc:
LLMDRouterCoordinatorSubsystem is the Prometheus subsystem for coordinator
metrics. Every metric declared in this package uses it.

operator_config.name: ModelUnknown
operator_config.doc:
ModelUnknown is the model_name label value for requests that carried no
model in the body (empty or absent). It is distinct from the cardinality
overflow value returned by boundModel once the cap fills.

operator_config.name: ErrBadRequest
operator_config.doc:
ErrBadRequest marks a step failure as caused by invalid client input rather
than an internal or upstream fault. Steps wrap it (with %w) when rejecting a
malformed request so the server can answer 400 instead of 502.

operator_config.name: ErrPipelineDone
operator_config.doc:
ErrPipelineDone is returned by a step to signal successful early exit.
The pipeline treats this as success and stops executing further steps.

operator_config.name: validRequestID
operator_config.doc:
validRequestID bounds a client-supplied x-request-id to alphanumerics and
dashes, at most 128 characters. handleInference replaces a header that fails
the match with a generated UUID before it reaches error responses; the
request-logging middleware redacts it. This keeps attacker-controlled content
out of both surfaces.

operator_config.name: errCacheMiss
operator_config.doc:
errCacheMiss signals that the conditional-decode cache probe returned 412.
It flows from the proxy's ModifyResponse to its ErrorHandler, which swallows
it so the miss can fall through to the rest of the pipeline.

operator_config.name: allowedImageContentTypes
operator_config.doc:
allowedImageContentTypes is the set of data URI media types a vision model
accepts. Non-image payloads (HTML, SVG, scripts, audio, video) are rejected
so they are not inlined and forwarded downstream.

operator_config.name: cgnatBlock
operator_config.doc:
cgnatBlock is the RFC 6598 carrier-grade NAT range, which net.IP has no
dedicated predicate for.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxDownloadSize
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxDownloadSize is the default cap for max_download_size, in megabytes.

operator_config.name: errBlockedAddress
operator_config.value: fmt.Errorf("address resolves to a blocked range: %w", pipeline.ErrBadRequest)
operator_config.doc:
errBlockedAddress marks a dial to a forbidden address. It wraps
pipeline.ErrBadRequest so the connection failure surfaced by http.Client.Do
(wrapped in *url.Error/*net.OpError, both of which Unwrap) classifies as a
client 4xx rather than a 502.

operator_config.name: maxErrorBodySize
operator_config.doc:
maxErrorBodySize caps how much of a non-2xx upstream response body is read
into memory, bounding OOM exposure to an adversarial upstream pod.

operator_config.name: DefaultScorerWeight
operator_config.doc: DefaultScorerWeight is the weight used for scorers referenced in the configuration without explicit weights.

operator_config.name: defaultCrossReplicaSyncInterval
operator_config.doc:
defaultCrossReplicaSyncInterval is the fallback cadence at which local
per-endpoint state is pushed to the syncer when none is configured.

operator_config.name: denyAllSpec
operator_config.doc:
denyAllSpec confines an unregistered plugin the same way as one that
declares nothing.

operator_config.name: ErrDuplicateExtractorType
operator_config.value: errors.New("duplicate extractor type configured for the same source")

operator_config.name: ErrNoDefaultProducer
operator_config.value: errors.New("no default producer found for missing data key")

operator_config.doc: compile-time type assertion

operator_config.name: activePortsAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
activePortsAnnotation is used to specify which ports on a pod should be considered
as active for inference traffic. The value should be a comma-separated list of port numbers.
Example: "8000,8001,8002"

operator_config.name: errPoolNotSynced
operator_config.value: errors.New("InferencePool is not initialized in data store")

operator_config.name: errRegistrationDropped
operator_config.value: errors.New("endpoint registration dropped: collector already registered or failed to start")
operator_config.doc:
errRegistrationDropped reports an endpoint that could not be tracked: its collector is
still registered from an earlier registration (an upsert overlapping an in-flight delete)
or failed to start. Callers match it with errors.Is to decide whether to retry.

operator_config.name: legacyGAIEActivePortsAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
legacyGAIEActivePortsAnnotation is the legacy GAIE active ports annotation key, kept for backward compatibility.

Deprecated: use activePortsAnnotation instead; this may be removed in a future release.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowIDEmpty
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowIDEmpty indicates that a flow specification was provided with an empty flow ID.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound indicates that a requested flow instance (a `ManagedQueue`) does not exist.

operator_config.name: ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle
operator_config.doc:
ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle indicates that a QueueItemHandle provided to a SafeQueue operation (e.g.,
SafeQueue.Remove()) is not valid for that queue, has been invalidated, or does not correspond to an actual item in
the queue.

operator_config.name: ErrPriorityBandNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrPriorityBandNotFound indicates that a requested priority band does not exist in the registry configuration.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueItemNotFound
operator_config.value: errors.New("queue item not found for the given handle")
operator_config.doc:
ErrQueueItemNotFound indicates that a SafeQueue.Remove(handle) operation did not find an item matching the
provided, valid QueueItemHandle. This can occur if the item was removed by a concurrent operation.

operator_config.name: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize
operator_config.doc: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize is the default size of a worker's incoming request buffer.

operator_config.name: defaultEvictionConfirmationGrace
operator_config.doc:
defaultEvictionConfirmationGrace covers the reclaiming stage (engine abort, KV GC, scrape,
staleness window) for the default utilization detector. Deployments pairing eviction with the
concurrency detector can lower it substantially.

operator_config.name: defaultEvictionConfirmationTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultEvictionConfirmationTimeout bounds how long an unconfirmed revocation can hold the
reclamation pacing gate closed.

operator_config.name: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval is the default frequency for scanning for expired items.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxRevocationsPerDecision
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxRevocationsPerDecision caps revocations per reclamation decision, bounding the
damage from mean-footprint misestimation.

operator_config.name: defaultNoEndpointRequestTTL
operator_config.doc:
defaultNoEndpointRequestTTL is the queue-wait budget applied while the candidate pool has no endpoints when
neither budget is configured. It is deliberately equal to `defaultRequestTTL`, so splitting the budget is opt-in:
sizing the two regimes apart (a cold start is minutes, a time-to-first-token SLO is seconds) is a
deployment-specific decision, not one a default can make.

operator_config.name: defaultRequestTTL
operator_config.doc:
defaultRequestTTL is the default Time-To-Live applied to queued requests when the configuration
does not specify one. It is a queue-wait budget: a request still undispatched after this long is
shed with a retryable backpressure signal instead of being served with severely degraded
time-to-first-token. With no client or gateway deadline (the well-lit guides configure no gateway
request timeout) it is the only bound on waiting against a pool that has endpoints; where such
deadlines exist and fire sooner, context cancellation evicts the request first.

operator_config.name: ErrProcessorBusy
operator_config.doc:
ErrProcessorBusy is a sentinel error returned by the processor's Submit method indicating that the processor's
internal buffer is momentarily full and cannot accept new work.

operator_config.name: maxCleanupWorkers
operator_config.doc:
maxCleanupWorkers caps the number of concurrent workers for background cleanup tasks. This prevents the processor
from overwhelming the Go scheduler with too many goroutines.

operator_config.name: PriorityQueueName
operator_config.doc:
PriorityQueueName identifies the priority queue implementation (used for benchmark labels).

This queue provides a concurrent-safe priority queue whose ordering is maintained by an internal
container/heap. Items are ordered by the configured OrderingPolicy, with the highest-priority
item (per the policy) at the head.

Each item's position in the heap is tracked on its handle, enabling O(log n) targeted removal.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting which flow's queue to service next.

operator_config.name: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting items within a single flow's queue.

operator_config.name: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef is the default policy to compute usage limit of a priority band dynamically.

operator_config.name: defaultFlowGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultFlowGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which an idle flow is garbage collected.
This also serves as the interval for the periodic garbage collection scan.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which a dynamically provisioned
priority band is garbage collected. Set to 2x flow GC timeout to ensure flows are cleaned up first.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes is the default byte-size capacity for a priority band if not explicitly
configured. It is set to 1 GB.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxRequests
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxRequests is the default request-count capacity for a priority band if not
explicitly configured. Together with the default request TTL (60s), it only binds when a band's
arrival rate under a dispatch halt exceeds maxRequests/TTL (~83 req/s); below that, TTL expiry
bounds occupancy first.

operator_config.name: ErrContextCancelled
operator_config.doc:
ErrContextCancelled indicates a request was evicted because its associated context (from
`FlowControlRequest.Context()`) was cancelled. This error typically wraps the underlying `context.Canceled` or
`context.DeadlineExceeded` error.

operator_config.name: ErrEvicted
operator_config.doc:
ErrEvicted is a sentinel error indicating a request was removed from a queue *after* being successfully enqueued,
but for reasons other than successful dispatch (e.g., TTL expiry, displacement). Errors returned by
`FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify post-queue eviction will wrap this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrEvicted)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowControllerNotRunning
operator_config.doc:
ErrFlowControllerNotRunning indicates that an operation could not complete or an item was evicted because the
`controller.FlowController` is not running or is in the process of shutting down.

When returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()`, this will be wrapped by `ErrRejected` (if rejection happens
before internal queuing) or `ErrEvicted` (if eviction happens after internal queuing).

operator_config.name: ErrNoEndpoints
operator_config.doc:
ErrNoEndpoints indicates that a request was rejected at the queue-capacity boundary while the candidate pool had no
endpoints. The queue acts as a scale-from-zero waiting room; when it fills with no backends to drain it, the
rejection reflects genuine unavailability rather than backpressure against a contended pool.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueAtCapacity
operator_config.doc: ErrQueueAtCapacity indicates that a request could not be enqueued because queue capacity limits were met.

operator_config.name: ErrRejected
operator_config.doc:
ErrRejected is a sentinel error indicating a request was rejected by the `controller.FlowController` *before* being
formally enqueued. Errors returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify pre-queue rejection will wrap
this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrRejected)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrTTLExpired
operator_config.doc: ErrTTLExpired indicates a request was evicted from a queue because its effective Time-To-Live expired.

operator_config.name: ErrIncompatiblePriorityType
operator_config.value: errors.New("incompatible priority score type for comparison")
operator_config.doc:
ErrIncompatiblePriorityType indicates that a FairnessPolicy attempted to compare items from two different flow
queues whose ItemComparators have different ScoreType values, making a meaningful comparison impossible.

operator_config.name: DefaultStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
DefaultStalenessThreshold defines the built-in threshold for considering data as stale.
If a request's data has not been read/written within this duration, it is reaped in the next
cleanup cycle. It applies when no process-wide override is set via SetDefaultStalenessThreshold.

operator_config.name: defaultCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultCleanupInterval defines the periodic interval that the cleanup goroutine uses to check for stale data.

operator_config.name: defaultStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
defaultStalenessThreshold is the process-wide default staleness threshold applied to new
PluginState instances. It may be overridden once at startup via SetDefaultStalenessThreshold.

operator_config.name: DefaultProducerRegistry
operator_config.doc:
DefaultProducerRegistry maps a data key to the default producer plugin name (same as type).
Populated via RegisterAsDefaultProducer.

operator_config.name: PluginsWithPluginDependencies
operator_config.doc: PluginsWithPluginDependencies maps plugin types to their configuration parser function, used to determine plugin dependencies

operator_config.name: Registry
operator_config.doc: Registry is a mapping from plugin type to Factory function.

operator_config.name: RegistryMetadata
operator_config.doc: RegistryMetadata maps a plugin type to its PluginMetadata.

operator_config.name: ErrNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrNotFound is the not found error message.

operator_config.name: StabilityAlpha
operator_config.doc: StabilityAlpha indicates an experimental plugin with no backwards-compatibility guarantees.

operator_config.name: StabilityBeta
operator_config.doc: StabilityBeta indicates a feature-complete plugin following the +2 minor release deprecation policy.

operator_config.name: StabilityStable
operator_config.doc: StabilityStable indicates a production-grade plugin guaranteed to be backwards compatible.

operator_config.name: ConditionalDecodeHandledAttributeKey
operator_config.doc:
ConditionalDecodeHandledAttributeKey is the request-attribute key a
PreRequest plugin sets when it has evaluated the "Prefer: if-available"
preference for a request. The director consults this after PreRequest
plugins run: a conditional-decode request that no plugin claimed is
rejected with 412 so misconfigurations (gate plugin forgotten) surface as a
fast fallback rather than a silent forward.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseClientDisconnect
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseClientDisconnect is a stream torn down under the EPP while the response was
in flight. A client disconnect is the most common reason; any teardown the EPP observes only
as a cancelled stream (Envoy drain or restart, an upstream reset, the EPP's own drain)
produces the same value, because the EPP cannot distinguish the reasons from its side of
the stream.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseError
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseError is a stream that ended without completing for any reason not otherwise
classified: a half-close that reaches the EPP before its cancellation propagates, or an
EPP-side failure.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseEvicted
operator_config.doc: TerminationCauseEvicted is a stream the EPP terminated to reclaim capacity.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseNatural
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseNatural is a stream the model server ended on its own, including responses
that deliver an error status in full.

operator_config.name: Affinity
operator_config.doc:
Affinity indicates a scorer that prefers endpoints with existing locality, such as kv-cache or session-related state,
and therefore tends to give higher scores to the same endpoints.

operator_config.name: Balance
operator_config.doc: Balance indicates a scorer that its preference is balanced between Affinity and Distribution.

operator_config.name: Distribution
operator_config.doc:
Distribution indicates a scorer that prefers spreading requests evenly across all candidate endpoints to avoid
hotspots and improve overall utilization.

operator_config.name: ModalityNone
operator_config.doc: ModalityNone is the mm.modality value when no multimodal content is present.

operator_config.name: InFlightLoadDataKey
operator_config.doc:
InFlightLoadDataKey carries the per-endpoint in-flight load snapshot used by
load-aware scorers. Populated by InFlightLoadProducer.Produce on each
candidate endpoint at the start of every scheduling cycle.

Represents the live, real-time load on the endpoint (tokens and requests),
injected dynamically and never overwritten during a scheduling cycle.

operator_config.name: UncachedRequestTokensDataKey
operator_config.doc:
UncachedRequestTokensDataKey carries the projected impact of the current request
on a specific endpoint. Populated statically during scheduling.

operator_config.name: GPUUtilizationDataKey

pool and incur higher overheads for every GET (e.g., socket initiation, certificate

operator_config.doc: UtilizationDetectorType is the unique identifier for this plugin.

staleWarnInterval bounds how often the detector logs about endpoints with missing or stale
metrics. Saturation is evaluated every dispatch cycle (~1ms), so the condition must be logged
on a time budget, never per evaluation.

operator_config.doc: domainRank maps by ordinal rank, ignoring numerical priority values.

operator_config.name: domainValue

operator_config.doc:
shape constants define the interpolation curve applied across the ceiling range.
Only "linear" is supported; additional shapes (sigmoid, exponential, step, etc.) may be added.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterPluginType
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterPluginType is the explicit cluster-scoped approx-prefix producer.

operator_config.name: minBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc:
minBlockSizeTokens is the floor applied to the block size returned by
GetBlockSize. The routing-side indexer keeps one LRU entry per (pod, block),
so very small block sizes cause gigabyte-scale memory growth at scale. 64
tokens is coarse enough to bound memory while still preserving useful
prefix-match signal. Defined as a var so tests in this package can lower it
to exercise prefix-match logic at small block sizes without leaking a knob
into the public configuration surface. See
https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1158.

operator_config.name: defaultBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc: defaultBlockSizeTokens is the default token block size (vLLM default is 16).

operator_config.name: defaultLRUCapacityPerServer
operator_config.doc:
defaultLRUCapacityPerServer is the default capacity of the LRU indexer per server.
The indexer is an approximation to the actual prefix LRU cache state on the model servers per server (pod).
A small capacity ensures a high accuracy of cache hit on the model server, but it will
increase the chance of false negatives. A high capacity does the opposite.
To properly size this, consider the sum of the total number of cache entries on all model
servers. Consider the llama3 8B model on a H100 80GB GPUs. The size of the model weight is
about 16GB. The remaining HBM used for caching prefixes is 64GB. Each
token is about 128KB in size, so we can cache 500K tokens. Using the default block size of 16
in vLLM, we will have 500K / 16 = 31.25K blocks.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixBlocks is the fallback block cap, consulted only when
MaxPrefixTokensToMatch is 0 and MaxPrefixBlocksToMatch is non-zero; the
default token cap otherwise supersedes it.
Two long requests with the same prefix up to this limit will be indistinguishable.
This parameter provides a trade-off between cache size, prefix matching speed and matching
accuracy. Use a small value if most requests are short to reduce cache size and speed up the
matching process. Use a large value if most requests are long to increase the matching accuracy.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixTokens
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixTokens caps prefix matching at the context window of large
production models (128K tokens, e.g. gpt-oss 120b), a reasonable upper bound
that covers the long-prompt use cases seen in production. It takes precedence
over defaultMaxPrefixBlocks: maxBlocks = defaultMaxPrefixTokens / blockSizeTokens.

operator_config.name: experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile
operator_config.doc:
experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile is a hardcoded profile name for prefill nodes.
In P/D disaggregation mode, the prefill and decode are usually represented as two different
scheduling profiles to pick the prefill and decode endpoints. This constant defines the
prefill profile name to ensure that the index is updated for the prefill endpoint and not
only for the primary endpoint that will initially handle the request.
This is hardcoded for now until we land on a canonical approach for plugins to identify
prefill and decode endpoints (See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/issues/2080)

operator_config.name: podActiveCheckInterval
operator_config.doc: podActiveCheckInterval is the interval at which we check if pods are still active.

operator_config.name: unlimitedPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
unlimitedPrefixBlocks is the block cap used when both MaxPrefixTokensToMatch
and MaxPrefixBlocksToMatch are 0. Prompt length is already bounded by the
model server's context window, so an absent cap matches at most one context
window of tokens.

operator_config.name: produceTimeoutMargin
operator_config.doc:
produceTimeoutMargin is added to the window so the director's per-producer
timeout does not cancel a request still waiting for its batch to seal.

operator_config.name: PluginType
operator_config.doc: PluginType is the unique identifier for the burst prefix cache producer plugin.

operator_config.name: balanceByRequests
operator_config.doc: balanceByRequests balances placement by request count (the default).

operator_config.name: balanceByTokens
operator_config.doc:
balanceByTokens balances placement by prefix-block (token) load, charging a
prefix only the blocks a replica must still prefill - blocks already held from
an earlier request sharing that prefix are free. Spreads long-prompt requests
so no replica saturates on stacked prefixes while shorter ones pack together.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixBlocks caps how many leading blocks form a group key.
Two prompts identical up to this many blocks are treated as one group.

operator_config.name: maxWindowDurationMs
operator_config.doc:
maxWindowDurationMs bounds the batch window. Every request waits up to this
long, so a misconfigured large value is rejected at construction rather than
stalling every request.

operator_config.name: unlimitedBatchSize
operator_config.doc:
unlimitedBatchSize is the MaxBatchSize sentinel that disables the
per-window cap on accumulated requests.

operator_config.name: unlimitedPerReplica

unlimitedPerReplica is the MaxPerReplica sentinel that disables the
per-replica cap, sending every sample of a group to a single replica.

request. It is deliberately a fixed value rather than the client's

LONG-vs-SHORT separation dominates, not to predict exact length.

operator_config.name: ShortOutputTokens
operator_config.doc:

(tool-call) request.

operator_config.name: UnknownOutputTokens
operator_config.doc:
UnknownOutputTokens is the flat output-token estimate for an UNKNOWN
request (no output-length signal), preserving the ranking invariant
SHORT (100) < UNKNOWN (1000) < LONG (4096).
TODO(outlen): replace with a dynamic estimate (e.g. per-pool running average
of observed CompletionTokens) in a follow-up PR.

operator_config.name: GatingModeDisabled
operator_config.doc:
GatingModeDisabled turns off revision gating while preserving any
configured header selectors.

operator_config.name: GatingModeMaxRole
operator_config.doc:
GatingModeMaxRole applies the same coverage check as GatingModeSum, sums
each required role across every covered revision, and selects the role
with the largest total. Every revision is then weighted by its Ready pod
count for that same role. RequireRoles order resolves equal totals.

operator_config.name: GatingModeSum
operator_config.doc:
GatingModeSum does two things:
  1. Drop any revision missing Ready pods on any listed role
     (rollout drift safety).
  2. Weighted-random-pick ONE surviving revision, weighted by the
     sum of Ready pod counts across every listed role, and keep
     only that revision's candidates.
Traffic converges on (sum(crossRolePods(rev)) / sum over all
revisions), independent of the picker downstream. The "sum" name
refers to the per-revision sum used as weight.
For A={prefill:2,decode:9} and B={prefill:1,decode:1}, the weights
are 11 and 2, producing shares of 11/13 and 2/13.

operator_config.name: ModePrefer
operator_config.doc:

operator_config.name: ModeStrict
operator_config.doc:

pipeline returns an error (503). Intentional under strict mode:
the client asked for something specific and we do not silently
substitute.

map[topoutil.Level]float64{
	topoutil.LevelHost:	1.00,
	topoutil.LevelRack:	0.20,
	topoutil.LevelZone:	0.05,
	topoutil.LevelRegion:	0.02,
	topoutil.LevelNone:	0.00,
}
operator_config.doc:
levelScores maps the tightest common topology level to its proximity
score, shaped by the KV-transfer bandwidth available at that level rather
than by even spacing: same host uses NVLink, same rack a NIC and a single
switch, and each looser level adds switch hops. Host dominates rack 5:1 and
zone 20:1 so co-location wins outright, while the looser levels still carry
enough signal to break ties among non-colocated candidates.

These ratios are hardcoded rather than configurable per level; if a real
deployment shows they are wrong, add per-level weight parameters then.

series set without limit and exhaust memory.

rewrite targets) are pinned: they always emit their real label and do not count
against the cap, so a flood of unconfigured names cannot displace a configured
model into the overflow bucket.

operator_config.name: pruneEngineKeyScript
operator_config.value:
redis.NewScript(`
	for i = 2, #KEYS do
		if redis.call('HLEN', KEYS[i]) > 0 then
			return 0
		end
	end
	redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
	return 1
`)
operator_config.doc:
pruneEngineKeyScript atomically deletes an engine key mapping only if all
associated request key hashes are empty. This prevents a TOCTOU race where a
concurrent Add could insert into a request key between checking and deleting.
KEYS[1] = engine key ("engine:<hash>"), KEYS[2..N] = request key hashes.

operator_config.name: pruneRequestKeyScript

redis.NewScript(`
	local hashLen = redis.call('HLEN', KEYS[1])
	if hashLen == 0 then
		redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
		return 1
	end
	return 0
`)
operator_config.doc: pruneRequestKeyScript atomically deletes a request key hash if it contains no pods.

podIdentifierLabel is the label key carried by the per-pod kvevents metrics.
Keeping it as a constant localizes label-schema changes to this package.

operator_config.name: routerSubsystem
operator_config.doc:
routerSubsystem is the router's standard EPP metrics subsystem. New metrics
are emitted under it; the legacy kvcache_* names are retained as deprecated
aliases so existing scrapers keep working during the migration.

operator_config.name: TracerScope
operator_config.doc:
TracerScope is the OTel instrumentation scope for spans emitted by the
kvevents event pipeline.

operator_config.doc: EngineTypeSGLang selects the SGLang adapter.

operator_config.name: EngineTypeVLLM

operator_config.doc: Common event type tags shared across engine adapters.

operator_config.name: sglangBlockStoredFieldCount
operator_config.doc:
Expected field counts for SGLang msgpack array structs.
SGLang uses the same positional wire format as vLLM but may omit trailing optional fields
via omit_defaults=True in msgspec.
See: sglang/srt/disaggregation/kv_events.py (BlockStored, BlockRemoved classes).

operator_config.name: sglangBlockStoredMinFields
operator_config.doc: Minimum required fields (excluding trailing optional ones).

operator_config.name: noDataParallelRank
operator_config.doc:
noDataParallelRank is the sentinel data-parallel rank used in a dedup scope.

On current main the index identity (kvblock.PodEntry) is pod-level and does
NOT distinguish data-parallel ranks, so every scope uses this sentinel and
reference counts aggregate across ranks — which is exactly what the pod-level
index requires (a block is still resident on the pod until every rank has
removed it). The value matches PR #370's NoDataParallelRank (-1) convention.

TODO(#370): once DataParallelRank is propagated onto EventBatch and into
PodEntry, source the rank from the event in pool.go so the dedup scope
becomes DP-aware in lockstep with the (then DP-aware) index identity. No
change to this file is required — only the scope construction at the call
sites.

operator_config.name: noGroupIdx
operator_config.doc:
noGroupIdx is the sentinel groupIdx used in a dedup scope when an event
carries no KV-cache group. It mirrors the "no group" PodEntry state
(HasGroup=false), so grouped and ungrouped copies of the same block hash are
reference-counted independently — matching how the index treats them as
distinct entries. Real event group indices are non-negative (the engine
adapters reject a negative group_idx), so this sentinel cannot collide with a
genuine group.

operator_config.name: EventTypeAllBlocksCleared
operator_config.doc: EventTypeAllBlocksCleared indicates entire cache was cleared.

operator_config.name: EventTypeBlockRemoved
operator_config.doc: EventTypeBlockRemoved indicates blocks were evicted from cache.

operator_config.name: EventTypeBlockStored
operator_config.doc: EventTypeBlockStored indicates blocks were added to cache.

operator_config.name: disabledSpan
operator_config.doc:
disabledSpan stands in for a real span when event tracing is off. A single
package-level value keeps the default path free of allocation while call
sites use the span unconditionally.

operator_config.doc: Multimodal content types that need encoder processing.

operator_config.doc: tracerScope is the OTel instrumentation scope for the sidecar proxy.

operator_config.name: finishReasonLength
operator_config.doc: finishReasonLength is the finish reason when max_tokens was reached.

operator_config.name: dnsLookupFailuresTotal
operator_config.doc:
dnsLookupFailuresTotal counts failed request-path DNS lookups (which then
fall back to the last-known-good IP or, on cold start, the raw spec).

operator_config.name: dnsReresolveTotal
operator_config.doc:
dnsReresolveTotal counts successful request-path DNS re-resolutions of
MoRI-IO peer host specs (one per actual lookup, not per request; lookups
coalesced by singleflight count once).

operator_config.name: envMoRIIOMetricsAddr
operator_config.doc:
envMoRIIOMetricsAddr is a backward-compatible fallback for enabling the
Prometheus scrape endpoint. When set to a listen address (e.g. ":9090") and
the --metrics-port flag is unset, the sidecar serves the shared
controller-runtime metrics registry (which carries the moriio_dns_* counters)
at /metrics on that address. The --metrics-port flag takes precedence. Empty
(with no flag) disables it. Kept on a separate address so it never clashes
with the data-plane proxy port.

operator_config.name: moriioDNSSubsystem
operator_config.doc:
moriioDNSSubsystem is the Prometheus subsystem prefix for the MoRI-IO
request-path DNS re-resolution metrics. Full names are
moriio_dns_reresolve_total, moriio_dns_ip_changed_total, and
moriio_dns_lookup_failures_total.

operator_config.name: MoRIIOFeatureEnabled
operator_config.doc:
MoRIIOFeatureEnabled controls whether MoRI-IO WRITE-mode and Wide-EP
features are available. Set to false to keep the feature dormant until
full validation and CI integration is complete in a future RC.

When false, any attempt to use --moriio-write-mode or related flags will
fail with a clear error message directing users to wait for the feature
to be officially released.

AMD-MoRI-IO: Feature enabled for 1P1D (DP=EP=8) intra-node Wide-EP
and 2P2D (DP=EP=16) inter-node Wide-EP with LeaderWorkerSet support.

operator_config.name: defaultMoRIIOParallelDecodeWaitTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultMoRIIOParallelDecodeWaitTimeout backstops the parallel WRITE
dispatch: it bounds how long the decode leg waits on the prefill outcome
(and thus KV) before being cancelled, so a hung/failed prefill fails the
request instead of hanging. Prefill in parallel dispatch is capped to one
token, so it normally resolves well within this window.

operator_config.name: requestFieldRemoteDPRankOverride
operator_config.doc:
requestFieldRemoteDPRankOverride tells the decode-side connector to use
the sidecar's remote_dp_rank verbatim rather than recomputing its own hash.

operator_config.name: requestFieldRemoteDecoder
operator_config.doc:
OffloadingConnector kv_transfer_params fields. The role is encoded by the
nesting key, named for the remote party it describes: "remote_decoder" on
the prefiller leg, "remote_prefiller" on the decoder leg, "remote_kv_source"
for a symmetric cached-prefix pull.

operator_config.name: requestFieldRemoteNotifyPort
operator_config.doc:
MoRI-IO WRITE-mode kv_transfer_params fields, populated by the sidecar
so the prefill engine can push KV to decode via RDMA Write.

operator_config.name: requestHeaderDataParallelRank
operator_config.doc:
requestHeaderDataParallelRank pins a request to a specific vLLM
data-parallel rank, set on both legs of a disagg pair (see pickDPRank).

operator_config.name: defaultResolveTTL
operator_config.doc:
defaultResolveTTL bounds how long a resolved peer IP is cached before the
next request-time lookup re-resolves it. Kept short so a peer pod that
restarts with a new IP is picked up within one TTL window, but long enough
that steady-state request handling does not perform a DNS lookup per call.

operator_config.name: defaultResolveTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultResolveTimeout bounds a single DNS lookup on the request path so a
slow or hanging resolver cannot stall request handling indefinitely. On
timeout the resolver falls back to the last-known-good IP (or the raw spec).

operator_config.name: envMoRIIODNSResolveTTLSeconds
operator_config.doc:
envMoRIIODNSResolveTTLSeconds overrides the peer-IP re-resolution TTL (in
seconds). Operators can widen or tighten the window without a rebuild.

operator_config.name: envMoRIIODNSResolveTimeoutSeconds
operator_config.doc:
envMoRIIODNSResolveTimeoutSeconds overrides the per-lookup DNS timeout (in
seconds). Bounds how long a single request-path resolution may block before
falling back to the last-known-good IP (or the raw spec).

operator_config.name: BundleVersion
operator_config.doc:
BundleVersion is the value used for labeling the CRD bundle version.
Defaults to "main-dev" for development builds. Set via -ldflags at release time via Github workflow.

operator_config.name: BundleVersionAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
BundleVersionAnnotation is the annotation key used in llm-d CRDs to specify
the installed bundle version.

prometheus_metrics.help: Total failed MoRI-IO peer DNS lookups on the request path.

prometheus_metrics.help: Total successful request-path re-resolutions of MoRI-IO peer DNS names.
